note.after_visit_summary: Your psoriasis has gotten worse and covers about 12 percent of your body. The red, scaly patches on your elbows, knees, lower back, and scalp are moderate to severe. Your joints look fine. We are adding a new medicine for your scalp and will start a weekly shot once your insurance is approved and your blood tests come back. Keep taking your amlodipine 5 mg each morning. Use the clobetasol ointment on your body patches twice a day, but only for 2 weeks at a time, then stop for 1 week. Use the clobetasol scalp solution once at night. Do not get any live vaccines, but you should get the flu shot this fall. If you ever get joint pain, swelling, or morning stiffness, call us right away. We will contact you with your lab results. Follow up in 6 weeks, or sooner for your first injection once everything is approved.
